messages:
nina.patel: incident-bot paging: high error rate detected for /v1/generate (5xx spike) in us-west-2. Alert threshold crossed 3m ago — 12% 5xx, p50 latency 420ms, p95 2.3s. Paging on-call.
incident-bot: [ALERT] service=redwood-runtime severity=critical hostpool=us-west-2 metric=5xx_rate value=0.12 window=180s
mike.chen: oncall here, looking. any known deploys in last 30m?
alex.rivera: not from runtime team. eng-releases shows a canary for batching-controller 2026-03-14T01:05:12 (small). could be related.
sam_oncall: i'm joining. running quick prom query to confirm: `sum(rate(http_responses_total{code=~"5..",route="/v1/generate",region="us-west-2"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",region="us-west-2"}[5m]))`
alex.rivera: output: ~0.115 -> matches. also seeing queue_depth metric on scheduler pods climb: scheduler_queue_length{pool="gpt-large-usw2"} ~ 4300 (baseline 50-200)
nina.patel: yikes that's HOL territory. which request shapes are at head? `top_requests` shows some large seq_len=4096 batch jobs.
mike.chen: logs show repeated timeouts in gateway: `upstream_timeout while proxying` and many gateway 504s. head-of-line blocking from huge-context inference apparently preventing smaller requests from being scheduled.
incident-bot: triggered runbook: /runbooks/scheduler-hol-blocking.md — recommended mitigations: 1) enable short-request prioritization 2) temporarily reject/route long-context requests 3) scale scheduler workers
sam_oncall: starting mitigation step 1: enabling priority policy. patching config: `PATCH /admin/configs/pool/gpt-large-usw2` payload `{ "priority_policy": "size-aware", "small_request_threshold_tokens": 512 }` (via internal admin API)
alex.rivera: applied. will also reduce batch_window_ms from 15 -> 5 to favor latency. command: `adminctl set-config --pool gpt-large-usw2 batching.batch_window_ms=5`
mike.chen: applied both. watching metrics.
incident-bot: config change observed by autoscaler. scheduler pods: 6 -> 9 requested. but queue is still with HOL items.
julia_cs: customer impact check: Support queue shows ~18 customers affected with increased errors, 2 enterprise customers reporting timeouts. need to notify affected customers proactively after initial mitigation.
nina.patel: next mitigation: divert long-context requests to a degraded model shard (long-context-legacy) with independent queue to avoid blocking. can we flip routing rule?
alex.rivera: yes, creating routing rule: `POST /admin/routing/override` `{ "match": "ctx_tokens>2048 && route==/v1/generate", "target": "long-context-legacy", "reason": "mitigate HOL" }`
mike.chen: rule applied. verifying traffic split: short requests now 84% throughput, long-context rerouted ~16%.
sam_oncall: queue depth dropping — scheduler_queue_length now ~320 and trending down. 5xx rate dropped to ~3.5%.
incident-bot: note: some long-context requests are stateful and customers may observe degraded quality. Julia please prepare the customer advisory: brief, apologetic, action items, ETA.
julia_cs: drafting. will send to affected customers with note that we rerouted long-context requests and are investigating root cause; offer to assist with retries and adapt prompts.
alex.rivera: running deeper diagnostics: observed that the batching-controller admitted extremely large batches because admission check for max_token_budget was missed after the canary. there is a bug: admission ignores per-request token limit when packer enabled. log sample:
```
2026-03-14T01:12:03Z batching-controller WARN admit() accepted batch size=48 total_tokens=214748
2026-03-14T01:12:03Z scheduler ERROR enqueue() backlog=4312 head_request_id=abcd1234 tokens=4096
```
nina.patel: ok we have root cause candidate — admission bug + aggressive packer created giant batches that tie up GPU memory and KV cache, causing HOL blocking and timeouts.
mike.chen: immediate remedial action: rollback canary for batching-controller to previous stable (v2026-03-13.3). issuing rollback now: `kubectl -n runtime set image deployment/batching-controller batching-controller=redwood/batching-controller:v2026-03-13.3`
sam_oncall: rollback triggered. controllers restarting.
incident-bot: deploybot: rollback started at 1792063660, status: rolling. expected stable in ~45s.
alex.rivera: also pushing hotfix to admission check: patch that enforces per-request max_tokens and disables packer for a minute: `PR #4892` (hotfix) — will deploy after we confirm rollback.
mike.chen: rollback completed. scheduler_queue_length now ~90. error rate down to 1.1%. gateway 504s reduced dramatically.
julia_cs: sent update to customers: summary + mitigation + apology. asked customers to open priority ticket if they still see issues.
nina.patel: great. creating incident ticket (INC-20260314-17) and assigning to eng-runtime & eng-sre for postmortem and long-term fix. Please add any follow-ups: hotfix deploy, stronger regression tests for packer/admission, add circuit-breaker when queue_depth>1000.
alex.rivera: adding to ticket: reproduce steps, logs, canary diff, PR link, config changes applied during mitigation, customer impact summary.
sam_oncall: recommending we add an automated HOL detector that triggers temporary routing and packer disable when head_age > X and queue_depth>Y.
mike.chen: agreed. will own action to add rollout gating around packer changes + canary traffic threshold checks.
incident-bot: incident severity: S2 -> downgraded to S3 after rollback and customer impact limited. auto-note: escalate to on-call manager if regressions within 24h.
nina.patel: final checks — logs look healthy, all greenish for last 5m. anyone still seeing errors?
alex.rivera: nothing from runtime. closing immediate tasks.
julia_cs: follow-up email scheduled in 1h with customers and CSMs.
nina.patel: thanks team. postmortem owners: alex.rivera (cause/technical), julia_cs (customer comms), mike.chen (rollout & deploy controls). we'll meet tomorrow 09:30 to review and assign action items. :thumbsup:
mike.chen: thanks all. good catch on HOL detection idea.
incident-bot: incident closed for now at 1792063920. record saved to incidents/inc-1792063456.json
